quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle down.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should consider:

options.text: Whether or not other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether or not other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that lets other drivers see you and gives you enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when safe, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you—their lights help light the road and show bumps ahead.

questions.question: Before every ride, check all of the following except the:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and reapply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and reapply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and then reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
Pre-ride checks performed only by a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more frequently. Do a full check before every ride.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Brake harder and faster than usual.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, apply the brakes gently and carefully.

questions.question: When it starts raining, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Happen because passengers distract the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have ridden their bike for less than six months. Be very careful when riding a new motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To stay safe, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide what to handle first. Always use your headlight so others can see you. Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay out of the left part of your lane.
Always stay out of the right part of your lane.
Always stay out of the middle of your lane.

questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move around in your lane based on road conditions and what is safest at that moment.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past it.
Move to the shoulder instead of riding over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving on rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weaving is more dangerous than just riding straight.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your riding ability:

options.text: At amounts well below the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just slightly above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At amounts well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Your riding skills become impaired well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: To turn your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlebar grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because that is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than a walking pace, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pushing the grip in the direction you want to turn makes your motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, the best approach is to:

options.text: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider starts to pass.
Have several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal that no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish their pass and get back in formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: You need more space when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, as shown in the image?

options.text: The group will exit at the next ramp.

questions.explanation: Hand signals help groups communicate while riding. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger, it means all riders should move into a single-file line.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they will not fall behind the group, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: In a group ride, the best way to stay close together while keeping safe distance is to ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space for safety. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects many safety factors. It helps you see and be seen better, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. However, lane position does not help you go faster.
